subject: Follow-up: Per-unit cost probe + hyperscaler comparison — next tests
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Mills <lauren.mills@stratus.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Per-unit cost probe + hyperscaler comparison — next tests

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum:

What we heard (from Stratus):
- Target workload: high-volume chat assistant (~1.2B tokens/month expected after ramp).
- Tight latency requirement for P95 (<= 300ms for short turn prompts).
- Primary concern: predictable per-token economics across bursts and caching behavior.

What Redwood will run next (proposal):
1) Unit economics matrix: run 1M-token synthetic runs across three configs to report $/1M tokens
   - Hosted API (Redwood default runtime) — batching: [1, 64, 256], cache: warm vs cold
   - Dedicated (pinned pool) — same batching matrix; include reserved vs burst pricing assumptions
   - Competitor baselines — OpenAI/Azure OpenAI and Google Vertex AI (requesting same model family or closest equivalent)
2) Cache-hit sensitivity: measure effective token cost at cache hit rates {0%, 25%, 50%, 75%} with prefix reuse patterns you described.
3) Latency tail: capture P50/P95/P99 for each config and per-batch size.
4) Quality parity spot-checks: 200 prompt eval set (you shared) to confirm responses are comparable across models.

Deliverables / timing:
- Cost matrix spreadsheet + logs (CSV) 
- Short one-page executive summary with recommended config and delta vs hyperscalers
- Proposed next customer-facing test harness so you can reproduce results

Can you confirm you’re happy with that scope and whether Stratus can supply a representative 200-prompt eval set (or we can use the redacted set from today)? If yes, we’ll schedule the 1M-token runs starting Monday and share interim numbers by mid next week.

Attachments: redwood-unit-econ-probe-brief.pdf (shortmethods + assumptions)

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0182
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Mills <lauren.mills@stratus.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Per-unit cost probe + hyperscaler comparison — next tests

Irene / Marissa —

Thanks Irene for the tidy plan. A few operational clarifications and additions from the infra/econ side so the runs are apples-to-apples:

1) Model parity: we should pin to the same architecture family (e.g., Llama-2-like transformer at 13B) and run both float16 and 4-bit quantized variants if the competitor offers quantized endpoints. That affects cost heavily.

2) Batching matrix refinement: instead of raw [1,64,256], run [1, 16, 64, 128] and include a continuous-batching target (avg batch size observed in production for a sample 24h trace Lauren can provide).

3) KV/prefix cache test: run warm-state tests with a 25k token rolling prefix and cold-state where KV cache misses each session. Measure tokens saved and incremental latency.

4) Throughput / utilization: capture GPU utilization per run so we can normalize $/1M tokens against utilization (helpful for dedicated pricing).

5) Hyperscaler baseline: ask Stratus for any existing usage with OpenAI/Azure/GCP (billing samples are ideal). If they can’t share billing, we’ll approximate using the same prompt set and request round-trip timings from their preferred endpoints.

6) Failure & fallback economics: include a small simulate of fallback traffic (10% of requests fall back to a cheaper model) to show blended $/token.

I’ll attach an example CSV schema for the logs we’ll need (see 1M-token-batch-logs-sample.csv). Infra will need the 200-prompt eval set and a sample 24h trace to calibrate the continuous-batching target.

If everyone is aligned I’ll kick the runs and reserve dedicated capacity for two 4-hour windows next Tue/Wed so runs finish quickly.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Mills <lauren.mills@stratus.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Per-unit cost probe + hyperscaler comparison — next tests

Couple of commercial notes to dovetail with Ben’s asks:

- When we present the $/1M token numbers, include both list pricing and a modeled committed discount (e.g., 20% reserved for Dedicated) so Stratus sees the delta between self-serve hosted and a committed Dedicated contract.
- Break out the economics into: compute-only (GPU hours normalized), infra overhead (network egress where applicable), and ops/license line items.
- Recommend a short slide that shows "when Dedicated makes sense" threshold (tokens/month vs cost crossover). That will help close the deal.

Irene — I can draft that slide once Ben provides the utilization-normalized $/1M metrics. Also please make sure we capture any API rate-limiting differences we hit during the competitor runs (those are a common objection).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Cloud Economics, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Per-unit cost probe + hyperscaler comparison — next tests

Irene / Ben / Marissa —

This scope looks good to me. We can provide a redacted 200-prompt set and a 24h trace of production traffic (anonymized); I’ll drop both into the Drive folder linked below by EOD Friday.

One ask from our procurement team: if you can include a short appendix with rough SLOs and the SLA differences between Hosted vs Dedicated (esp. scheduled maintenance windows and expected failover time), that will speed approvals on our side.

Irene — let me know the exact folder/place you want logs to land or if you prefer we share temporary credentials to a bucket.

Thanks — looking forward to the numbers.

Lauren Mills
Head of ML Infrastructure, Stratus Analytics
lauren.mills@stratus.com
